about: The missal prints this confession in full only once — here, in the priest's mouth — and gives the ministers' version as a single rubric: where the priest said “vobis, fratres” and “vos, fratres”, the ministers say “tibi, pater” and “te, pater”. Apart from those two places the two confessions are word for word the same. It is worth hearing what each calls the other: the priest addresses those before him as brothers, and they address him as father. He confesses first and alone, bowed low; the answer he will hear is the very formula he is about to say over them, only in the singular.

s01.narrative: The priest joins his hands and bows low; he makes the general confession first, alone.

s02.translation: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, brethren:

s03.translation: that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed:

s04.narrative: The priest strikes his breast three times — the gesture of contrition accompanies the words of self-accusation.

s05.translation: through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.

s06.translation: Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, brethren, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

w001.function: It opens the prayer and governs the long chain of datives that follows — I confess: to whom?

w002.function: The one confessed to — first of the chain of datives after “Confíteor” (w001). Compare “Deum” (w065) — the same word in the accusative, in a different role.

w005.function: The next addressee of the confession in the list.

w006.function: An adverb modifying a noun, unusually: “semper Virgo” — “ever Virgin” — a fixed Marian title treated as a unit.

w008.function: Agrees with the name that follows, “Michaéli” (w009).

w010.function: Apposition to “Michaéli” (w009): same case, because an apposition inherits the case of the noun it restates.

w016.function: Apposition to “Apóstolis” (w015) — the Apostles named one by one.

w021.function: Closes the list and adds its last members: those standing before the altar.

w022.function: The priest confesses to the people standing before him as well — plural, because he speaks to everyone present.

w023.function: Vocative, though in the plural it sounds the same as nominative and accusative: this is direct address, not another item in the list. The priest calls brethren those who will answer him “father”.

w024.function: Introduces the content of the confession: “that I have sinned” — though the classical “for I have sinned” still resonates here.

w025.function: A completed act whose effect endures — hence the confession.

w027.function: By what have I sinned — by thought; first of three ablatives of means: by thought, by word, by deed.

w032.function: The written form does not distinguish the nominative (culpă) from the ablative (culpā) — sense decides: ablative of cause, “through my fault”.

w037.function: The threefold “mea culpa” builds: fault — fault — greatest fault.

w038.function: The prayer's logical turn: having confessed, I now ask for intercession.

w039.function: It takes an accusative of the person plus an infinitive: I beseech whom — to do what. Hence the whole list now returns in the accusative.

w040.function: Agrees with “Maríam” (w041). Compare “beátæ” (w004): there dative after “Confíteor” (w001), here accusative after “precor” (w039).

w041.function: No longer the addressee of the confession but the one beseeched to intercede — object of “precor” (w039).

w043.function: Compare “Vírgini” (w007) — the same formula, there in the dative.

w058.function: Compare “vobis” (w022): the same people, a different case for a different role — there the ones confessed to, here the ones asked to pray.

w059.function: The vocative repeated from the first half — addressed to those standing before the altar.

w060.function: Infinitive in the construction “precor + accusative + infinitive”: I beseech you to pray. It carries the content of the petition.

w064.function: Accusative after “ad” (w063); the whole phrase “Dóminum Deum nostrum” stands in the accusative.

w065.function: Apposition to “Dóminum” (w064). Compare “Deo” (w002): the same word opened the prayer in the dative.
